# Catalog Publication Identity Observation

Bounded consumer migration within approved #2151/#2542. The catalog's shared
publication-identity refresh read entity_id with duplicated dialect SQL from
a raw pool. It now consumes the existing complete eventrecord reader on the
original native store. The optional public fixture bridge returns the exact
existing owner's event/found/error result; it introduces no second decoder,
read transaction, header projection or persistence owner.

Required canonical reads remain required. This consumer retains its distinct
optional missing behavior: absent rows and empty header identities leave its
cache unchanged. Read errors still fail the fixture; no error is treated as
absence. The event-ID trim, empty-input/no-owner guard, entity-ID trim and
mutex-protected update remain exact. Payload entity_id never replaces the
canonical envelope/header authority.

## Systematic Consumption And Proof

| Manifestation | Disposition and exact proof |
| --- | --- |
| Every successful catalog publication entering shared refresh | Moved to the existing canonical owner, one finite recipe. Real root-reply and evidence append/reopen roots execute both backends. |
| Payload disagrees with canonical entity header | Both-store focused proof deliberately differs payload/header and requires the canonical header in the cache, with no raw pool on the harness. |
| Missing event or empty requested identity | Both-store proof preserves prior cache evidence and cardinality; missing is not a fatal required read. |
| Malformed complete records, raw/foreign, canceled and closed owners | Existing canonical owner adversarial roots exercise the same unchanged private reader on both stores. |
| Wrong context/store/header, inverted missing result or lost mutex/cache assignment | Finite independent consumer oracle rejects each substitution. Optional bridge source must exactly consume the existing owner. |
| Other causal/catalog bulk readers and fixture constructors | Still explicit #2542 debt; this cohort does not claim to close them. |
